proposed_edits.new_string:
def _emit_set_inplace_update(
        self,
        recv: ir.Value,
        op_fn_name: str,
        arg_expr: "Expr",
    ) -> ir.Value:
        """In-place set.{intersection,difference,symmetric_difference}_update.

        CPython mutates ``recv`` in place (identity preserved) and returns
        None. There is no ``py_set_clear`` primitive, so: compute the result
        with the pure helper (which reads recv), snapshot recv's current
        members via ``py_set_items`` (a list), remove each from recv, then
        repopulate recv from the result via ``py_set_update``. ``result``
        holds its own references to the shared element objects, so removing
        recv's references does not free elements that the result still
        needs.
        """
        arg_obj = self._emit_as_object(arg_expr)
        result = self.builder.call(
            self.runtime[op_fn_name],
            [recv, arg_obj],
            name=self._fresh("set.inplace.result"),
        )
        snapshot = self.builder.call(
            self.runtime["py_set_items"],
            [recv],
            name=self._fresh("set.inplace.snapshot"),
        )
        fn = self.current_function
        n_val = self.builder.call(
            self.runtime["py_obj_len"],
            [snapshot],
            name=self._fresh("set.inplace.len"),
        )
        idx_slot = self._alloca_in_entry(_I64, name="set.inplace.idx.addr")
        self.builder.store(ir.Constant(_I64, 0), idx_slot)
        cond_bb = fn.append_basic_block(name=self._fresh("set.inplace.cond"))
        body_bb = fn.append_basic_block(name=self._fresh("set.inplace.body"))
        step_bb = fn.append_basic_block(name=self._fresh("set.inplace.step"))
        end_bb = fn.append_basic_block(name=self._fresh("set.inplace.end"))
        self.builder.branch(cond_bb)
        self.builder.position_at_end(cond_bb)
        cur = self.builder.load(idx_slot, name=self._fresh("set.inplace.idx"))
        cond = self.builder.icmp_signed(
            "<", cur, n_val, name=self._fresh("set.inplace.cond.i1"),
        )
        self.builder.cbranch(cond, body_bb, end_bb)
        self.builder.position_at_end(body_bb)
        idx_box = self.builder.call(
            self.runtime["py_int_from_i64"],
            [cur],
            name=self._fresh("set.inplace.idx.box"),
        )
        elem = self.builder.call(
            self.runtime["py_obj_getitem"],
            [snapshot, idx_box],
            name=self._fresh("set.inplace.elem"),
        )
        self.builder.call(self.runtime["py_set_remove"], [recv, elem])
        self.builder.branch(step_bb)
        self.builder.position_at_end(step_bb)
        nxt = self.builder.add(
            cur, ir.Constant(_I64, 1), name=self._fresh("set.inplace.idx.next"),
        )
        self.builder.store(nxt, idx_slot)
        self.builder.branch(cond_bb)
        self.builder.position_at_end(end_bb)
        self.builder.call(self.runtime["py_set_update"], [recv, result])
        return self._emit_none_literal()
    def _spread_into_set(self, dst_set: ir.Value, src_expr: "Expr") -> None:
proposed_edits.note: New helper inserted directly before _spread_into_set (modeled on it). Uses only already-compiled runtime fns: py_set_intersection/difference/symmetric_difference, py_set_items, py_obj_len, py_int_from_i64, py_obj_getitem, py_set_remove, py_set_update. _emit_as_object/_alloca_in_entry are already used in this file.

Declare py_set_items so the frontend can call it. The function ALREADY EXISTS in the compiled runtime (pcc/runtime/py/py_set.py:374 @c_abi_export('py_set_items'), and the C mirror) and returns a real list — only the frontend ABI declaration is missing. No archive rebuild needed.

proposed_edits.new_string:
# A ``*args`` / ``**kwargs`` splat reaches here as a sentinel
        # Call(Name("*"|"**"), ...). _emit_as_object cannot evaluate that
        # sentinel as a value (it would look up a variable named "*" and
        # raise ``NameError: name '*'``). The exception-args persistence is
        # only meaningful for explicit positional args; skip it entirely
        # when a splat is present rather than crashing. (Properly forwarding
        # a splat into a builtin base's __init__ -- e.g. dict/list subclasses
        # like defaultdict/Counter -- is a separate, larger gap.)
        for a in args:
            if (
                isinstance(a, Call)
                and isinstance(a.func, Name)
                and a.func.ident in ("*", "**")
            ):
                return
        fd = getattr(self, "current_func_def", None)
        if fd is None or not fd.args:
            return
        self_name = fd.args[0].name or "self"

confirmed_gaps.observed: Runtime crash: TypeError raised from Counter.__getitem__ -> self.get(key, 0) (pcc/stdlib/collections.py:67-68). Even a present key (c['a'] after c['a']=3) raises. CPython prints 3/2/0.
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: Counter subclasses dict and its __getitem__ calls self.get(key, 0). pcc has no model for a class that subclasses a builtin (dict): the dict storage/methods are not inherited by the instance. self has static type ClassType(Counter) (type_infer.py self_ty), so 'self.get(...)' is NOT dispatched as a user method (Counter.info.methods has no 'get' -- it is inherited from dict) and ends up routed to a native dict helper py_dict_get_default(self_instance, ...) (dict_lowering.py:221-238) whose receiver is a PY_TYPE_INSTANCE, not a PY_TYPE_DICT, so the runtime raises TypeError. Equivalently a standalone 'class MyDict(dict): pass' that calls d.get(k,0) forces a libpython fallback (probes ds3_02a/ds3_02b: PCC-PY-COMPILE-001), confirming there is no native dict-subclass support. This is a substantial subsystem gap (builtin-subclass instance must carry dict storage and inherit dict's get/__getitem__/__setitem__/update/etc.), not a bounded one-edit fix; the same missing model defeats defaultdict and OrderedDict. Recorded with low confidence and no speculative edit because any correct fix changes the class/builtin-subclass object model and the dict-method receiver-type dispatch, which is high-risk to patch blind and must go through the bootstrap gate. The human should scope a dict-subclass storage model (instance backed by a native dict + method inheritance) as a dedicated task.
